rounds.response: Findings: Ms. Rivera purchased a Northbridge ProLine NP‑15X on November 18; within three months she reported recurrent random shutdowns, freezes, and data corruption; she returned the unit to Northbridge’s service center on two occasions but the same failures recurred thereafter, and the record shows multiple documented service attempts and error screenshots. Conclusion: Given the short time from purchase and two unsuccessful in‑warranty repair attempts, the device is reasonably treated as nonconforming and Ms. Rivera is entitled to a remedy beyond further troubleshooting. Order: Northbridge shall, within 14 calendar days of this determination, either (a) provide Ms. Rivera a new, equivalent laptop of equal or greater specifications and warranty at no charge, or (b) issue a full refund of the purchase price shown on the invoice upon return of the unit — Ms. Rivera may elect which remedy. Northbridge shall also reimburse documented, reasonable shipping costs and other documented out‑of‑pocket expenses directly related to the two prior service shipments, and shall not impose any usage, restocking, or similar deductions. This determination is binding; the case will be closed when Northbridge submits verifiable proof of compliance or will be escalated by the platform if compliance is not completed within the 14‑day period.
